spots.name: St Patrick's Cathedral
spots.summary: Saint Patrick's Cathedral in Dublin, Ireland is the national cathedral of the Church of Ireland. Christ Church Cathedral, also a Church of Ireland cathedral in Dublin, is designated as the local cathedral of the Diocese of Dublin and Glendalough.

spots.name: Dublin Castle
spots.summary: Dublin Castle is a major Irish government complex, conference centre, and tourist attraction. It is located off Dame Street in central Dublin.

spots.name: Spire of Dublin

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Spire of Dublin, alternatively titled the Millennium Spire or the Monument of Light, is a large, stainless steel, pin-like monument 120 metres (390 ft) in height, located on the site of the former Nelson's Pillar on O'Connell Street, the main thoroughfare of Dublin, Ireland.

spots.name: Christ Church Cathedral, Dublin
spots.summary: Christ Church Cathedral, more formally The Cathedral of the Holy Trinity, is the cathedral of the United Dioceses of Dublin and Glendalough and the cathedral of the ecclesiastical province of the United Provinces of Dublin and Cashel in the (Anglican) Church of Ireland.

spots.name: Leinster House

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Leinster House is the seat of the Oireachtas, the parliament of Ireland. Originally, it was the ducal palace of the Dukes of Leinster.

spots.name: Samuel Beckett Bridge
spots.summary: Samuel Beckett Bridge is a cable-stayed swingbridge in Dublin, Ireland that joins Sir John Rogerson's Quay on the south side of the River Liffey to Guild Street and North Wall Quay in the Docklands area.

spots.name: Nelson's Pillar
spots.summary: Nelson's Pillar was a large granite column capped by a statue of Horatio Nelson, built in the centre of what was then Sackville Street in Dublin, Ireland. Completed in 1809 when Ireland was part of the United Kingdom, it survived until March 1966, when it was severely damaged by explosives planted by Irish republicans.

photo.author: Fisher, H. Son and Co; George Petrie; R. Winkles

spots.name: Ha'penny Bridge
spots.summary: The Ha'penny Bridge, known later for a time as the Penny Ha'penny Bridge, and officially the Liffey Bridge, is a pedestrian bridge built in May 1816 over the River Liffey in Dublin, Ireland. Made of cast iron, the bridge was cast in Shropshire, England.

spots.name: Kilmainham Gaol
spots.summary: Kilmainham Gaol is a former prison in Kilmainham, Dublin. Opened in the late 18th century as the County of Dublin Gaol, it is now a museum run by the Office of Public Works.

spots.name: St Stephen's Green
spots.summary: St Stephen's Green is a garden square and public park located in the city centre of Dublin, Ireland. The current landscape of the park was designed by William Sheppard. It was officially re-opened to the public on Tuesday, 27 July 1880 by Lord Ardilaun.

photo.author: Dronepicr (edited by King of Hearts) Edit corrects CA and sharpens image

spots.name: National Gallery of Ireland
spots.summary: The National Gallery of Ireland houses the national collection of Irish and European art. It is located in the centre of Dublin with one entrance on Merrion Square, beside Leinster House, and another on Clare Street. It was founded in 1854 and opened its doors ten years later.

spots.name: St Mary's Cathedral
spots.summary: St Mary's Cathedral, formerly known as St Mary's Pro-Cathedral, is a cathedral and is the episcopal seat of the Catholic Archbishop of Dublin and Primate of Ireland.

spots.name: Glasnevin Cemetery
spots.summary: Glasnevin Cemetery is the national cemetery of Ireland, located on the Northside of Dublin. More than 1.5 million people are buried in the cemetery, including a number of notable historical figures.

spots.name: National Museum of Ireland

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Museum of Ireland is Ireland's leading museum institution, with a strong emphasis on national and some international archaeology, Irish history, Irish art, culture, and natural history.

spots.name: Phoenix Park
spots.summary: The Phoenix Park, previously stylised as Phœnix Park, is a large public urban park in Dublin, Ireland, lying 2–4 kilometres (1.2–2.5 mi) west of the city centre, north of the River Liffey. Its 11 kilometres (6.8 mi) perimeter wall encloses 707 hectares of recreational space.

spots.name: O'Connell Bridge
spots.summary: O'Connell Bridge is a road bridge spanning the River Liffey in Dublin, Ireland, which joins O'Connell Street to D'Olier Street, Westmoreland Street and the south quays.

spots.name: Library of Trinity College Dublin

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Library of Trinity College Dublin is the main library that serves Trinity College, and is the largest library in Ireland. It is a legal deposit or "copyright library", which means that publishers in Ireland must deposit a copy of all their publications there without charge.

spots.name: Wellington Monument
spots.summary: The Wellington Monument, or sometimes the Wellington Testimonial, is an obelisk located in the Phoenix Park, Dublin, Ireland.

spots.name: Guinness Storehouse
spots.summary: Guinness Storehouse is a tourist attraction at St. James's Gate Brewery in Dublin, Ireland. Since opening in 2000, it has received over twenty million visitors.

spots.name: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum
spots.summary: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, located in Dublin's Docklands, covers the history of the Irish diaspora and emigration to other countries. The museum, which is privately owned, was designed by the London-based design firm Event Communications.

spots.name: Garden of Remembrance
spots.summary: The Garden of Remembrance is a memorial garden in Dublin dedicated to the memory of "all those who gave their lives in the cause of Irish Freedom". It is located in the northern fifth of the former Rotunda Gardens in Parnell Square, a Georgian square at the northern end of O'Connell Street.

spots.name: Famine
spots.summary: The Famine Memorial, officially titled Famine, is a memorial in Dublin, Ireland made by Rowan Gillespie. The memorial, which stands on Customs House Quay, is in remembrance of the Great Famine (1845–1852), which saw the population of the country halved through death and emigration.

spots.name: College Green
spots.summary: College Green is a three-sided plaza in the centre of Dublin, Ireland. On its northern side is the Bank of Ireland building, which until 1800 was Ireland's Parliament House. To its east stands Trinity College Dublin. To its south stands a series of 19th-century buildings.

spots.name: Hugh Lane Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Hugh Lane Gallery, and originally the Municipal Gallery of Modern Art, is an art museum operated by Dublin City Council and its wholly owned company, the Hugh Lane Gallery Trust. It is in Charlemont House on Parnell Square, Dublin, Ireland. Admission is free.

spots.name: Parnell Square
spots.summary: Parnell Square is a Georgian square sited at the northern end of O'Connell Street in the city of Dublin, Ireland. It is in the city's D01 postal district.

spots.name: Irish Museum of Modern Art

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Irish Museum of Modern Art, also known as IMMA, is Ireland's leading national institution for the collection and presentation of modern and contemporary art. It is located in Kilmainham, Dublin.

spots.name: Oscar Wilde Memorial Sculpture
spots.summary: The Oscar Wilde Memorial Sculpture is a collection of three statues in Merrion Square in Dublin, Ireland, commemorating Irish poet and playwright Oscar Wilde. The sculptures were unveiled in 1997 and were designed and made by Danny Osborne.

spots.name: Chester Beatty Library
spots.summary: The Chester Beatty Library, now known as the Chester Beatty, is a museum and library in the grounds of Dublin Castle, Ireland. It was established in 1953 at 20 Shewsbury Road, Dublin 4, to house the collections of mining magnate, Sir Alfred Chester Beatty.

spots.name: Dublin Zoo
spots.summary: Dublin Zoo, in Phoenix Park, is a zoo in Dublin, Ireland, and one of Dublin's most popular attractions. Established and designed in 1830 by Decimus Burton, it opened the following year. Today, it focuses on conservation projects, breeding programmes, and growing awareness for animals.

spots.name: Merrion Square
spots.summary: Merrion Square is a Georgian garden square on the southside of Dublin city centre.

spots.name: Anna Livia
spots.summary: Anna Livia is a bronze monument located in Croppies' Memorial Park in Dublin, Ireland. It was formerly located on O'Connell Street, where it lay as the centrepiece in a stone fountain. The monument is a personification of the River Liffey which runs through the city.

spots.name: Liberty Hall

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Liberty Hall, in Dublin, Ireland, is the headquarters of the Services, Industrial, Professional, and Technical Union (SIPTU). Designed by Desmond Rea O'Kelly, it was completed in 1965.

spots.name: National Library of Ireland

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The National Library of Ireland is Ireland's national library located in Dublin, in a building designed by Thomas Newenham Deane.

spots.name: St. James's Gate
spots.summary: St. James's Gate, located off the south quays of Dublin, on James's Street, was the western entrance to the city during the Middle Ages. During this time the gate was the traditional starting point for the Camino pilgrimage from Dublin to Santiago de Compostela in Galicia (Spain).

spots.name: Saint Anne's Park
spots.summary: Saint Anne's Park is a 240-acre (97 ha) public park situated between Raheny and Clontarf, suburbs on the northside of Dublin, Ireland. It is owned and managed by Dublin City Council.

spots.name: National Museum of Ireland – Archaeology

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The National Museum of Ireland, Kildare Street is a branch of the National Museum of Ireland located on Kildare Street in Dublin, Ireland, that specialises in Irish and other antiquities dating from the Stone Age to the Late Middle Ages.

spots.name: Dublinia
spots.summary: Dublinia is a historical recreation museum and visitor attraction in Dublin, Ireland, focusing on the Viking and Medieval history of the city. Dublinia is located in a part of Dublin's Christ Church Cathedral, known as the Synod hall.

spots.name: James Joyce Bridge
spots.summary: James Joyce Bridge is a road bridge spanning the River Liffey in Dublin, Ireland, joining the south quays to Blackhall Place on the northside.

spots.name: St. Audoen's Church, Dublin

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Audoen's Church is the church of the parish of Saint Audoen in the Church of Ireland, located south of the River Liffey at Cornmarket in Dublin, Ireland. This was close to the centre of the medieval city. The parish is in the Diocese of Dublin and Glendalough.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St. Audoen's Church, Dublin (Church of Ireland)

spots.name: Seán O'Casey Bridge
spots.summary: Seán O'Casey Bridge is a pedestrian swingbridge spanning the River Liffey in Dublin, Ireland, joining City Quay in the Grand Canal Docks area to North Wall Quay and the IFSC.

spots.name: Irish National War Memorial Gardens
spots.summary: The Irish National War Memorial Gardens is an Irish war memorial in Islandbridge, Dublin, dedicated "to the memory of the 49,400 Irish soldiers who gave their lives in the Great War, 1914–1918", out of a total of 206,000 Irishmen who served in the British forces alone during the war.

spots.name: Olympia Theatre
spots.summary: The Olympia Theatre, branded since 2021 for sponsorship purposes as the 3Olympia Theatre, is a concert hall and theatre venue in Dublin, Ireland, located on Dame Street.

spots.name: Dublin Writers Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Dublin Writers Museum was a museum of literary history in Dublin, Ireland. It opened in November 1991, and was hailed as an "iconic" museum in Dublin. It closed during the COVID-19 pandemic, and was brought to an end in 2022 without ever reopening.

spots.name: Fusiliers' Arch
spots.summary: The Fusiliers' Arch is a monument which forms part of the Grafton Street entrance to St Stephen's Green park, in Dublin, Ireland. Erected in 1907, it was dedicated to the officers, non-commissioned officers and enlisted men of the Royal Dublin Fusiliers who fought and died in the Second Boer War (1899–1902).

spots.name: St. Michan's Church

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: St. Michan's Church is a Church of Ireland church located in Church Street, Dublin, Ireland. The first Christian chapel on this site dated from 1095, and operated as a Catholic church until the Reformation.

spots.name: Gaiety Theatre
spots.summary: The Gaiety Theatre is a theatre on South King Street in Dublin, Ireland, off Grafton Street and close to St. Stephen's Green. It specialises in operatic and musical productions, with occasional dramatic shows.

spots.name: National Museum of Ireland – Natural History

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Museum of Ireland – Natural History, sometimes called the Dead Zoo, a branch of the National Museum of Ireland, is housed on Merrion Street in Dublin, Ireland. The museum was built in 1856 for parts of the collection of the Royal Dublin Society and the building and collection were later passed to the State.
spots.wikipediaTitle: National Museum of Ireland – Natural History

spots.name: Henry Street
spots.summary: Henry Street is located on Dublin's Northside and is one of the two principal shopping streets of Dublin.

spots.name: Dublin quays
spots.summary: The Dublin quays refers to the two roadways and quays that run along the north and south banks of the River Liffey in Dublin, Ireland. The stretches of the two continuous streets have several different names. However, all but two of the names share the same "quay" designation.

spots.name: John's Lane Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St. Augustine and St. John, commonly known as John's Lane Church, is a large Catholic church located on Thomas Street, Dublin, Ireland. It was opened in 1874 on the site of the medieval St. John's Hospital, founded c. 1180. It is served by the Augustinian Order of friars.

spots.name: St Andrew's Church, Dublin

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Andrew's Church is a former parish church of the Church of Ireland that is located in St Andrew's Street, Dublin, Ireland. After ceasing to be a church, it housed the main Dublin tourist office of Fáilte Ireland until 2014, and later underwent redevelopment with a view to reopening as a food hall.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St Andrew's Church, Dublin (Church of Ireland)

spots.name: Broom Bridge
spots.summary: Broom Bridge, also called Broome Bridge, and sometimes Brougham Bridge, is a bridge along Broombridge Road which crosses the Royal Canal in Cabra, Dublin, Ireland. Broome Bridge is named after William Broome, one of the directors of the Royal Canal company who lived nearby.

spots.name: Millennium Bridge
spots.summary: The Millennium Bridge is a pedestrian bridge spanning the River Liffey in Dublin, Ireland, joining Eustace Street in Temple Bar to the north quays.

spots.name: Grattan Bridge
spots.summary: Grattan Bridge is a road bridge spanning the River Liffey in Dublin, Ireland, and joining Capel Street to Parliament Street and the south quays.

spots.name: Mount Jerome Cemetery
spots.summary: Mount Jerome Cemetery & Crematorium is situated in Harold's Cross on the south side of Dublin, Ireland. Since its foundation in 1836, it has witnessed over 300,000 burials. Originally an exclusively Protestant cemetery, Roman Catholics have also been buried there since the 1920s.

spots.name: Marsh's Library

hours.note: Closed Tue, Sun

spots.summary: Marsh's Library formerly St. Sepulchre's Library, situated in St. Patrick's Close, adjacent to St. Patrick's Cathedral and St. Sepulchre's Palace, Dublin, Ireland is a well-preserved library of the late Renaissance and early Enlightenment. When it opened to the public in 1707 it was the first public library in Ireland.

spots.name: National Botanic Gardens
spots.summary: The National Botanic Gardens is a botanical garden in Glasnevin, 5 km north-west of Dublin city centre, Ireland. The 19.5 hectares are situated between Glasnevin Cemetery and the River Tolka where it forms part of the river's floodplain.

spots.name: Talbot Memorial Bridge
spots.summary: The Talbot Memorial Bridge, also known as the Matt Talbot Bridge, is a one-way road bridge spanning the River Liffey in Dublin, Ireland. The bridge marks the furthest point up to the Liffey to which tall ships may travel, as all bridges downriver of it are either swingbridges or bascule.

spots.name: Royal Hibernian Academy

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Royal Hibernian Academy of Arts (RHA) is an artist-based and artist-oriented institution in Ireland, founded in Dublin in 1823. Like many other Irish institutions, such as the Royal Irish Academy, the academy retained the word "Royal" after most of Ireland became independent as the Irish Free State in December 1922.

spots.name: Smithfield
spots.summary: Smithfield is an area on the Northside of Dublin, Ireland. Its focal point is a public square, formerly an open market and common, now officially called Smithfield Plaza, but known locally as Smithfield Square or Smithfield Market.

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.name: Outhouse LGBTQ+ Centre
spots.summary: Safe space for LGBTQ+ people, with community café, social and cultural events, resources and support services, a queer library, theatre and meeting spaces.

spots.name: The Formal Garden at The Royal Hospital Kilmainham
Peadar Kearney's

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Named for Peadar Ó Cearnaígh (1883-1942) who penned Amhráin na bhFiann, Ireland's national anthem, and was uncle to the three Behans, authors and prolific drinkers all. The pub is a great spot for pre- and post-gig drinks next to Olympia Theatre, with a young crowd and live music from up and coming Irish trad bands. Mostly tourists here but a nice spot to talk to other visitors.

spots.name: The Brazen Head

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Surely the oldest pub in Dublin, founded in 1198 - Ireland's oldest, in Athlone, is from 900 AD. Wonderful on warm, dry summer nights. Live trad music and friendly atmosphere. One of the bars is covered in signed currency notes, there's quite a collection but lacking any bitcoins.

spots.name: Bruxelles

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Lively pub founded in 1886. Spread over 3 bars the music is loud and the atmosphere is buzzing. Outside is a statue of Phil Lynott, from Irish rock band Thin Lizzy. For metal, rock and indie music go downstairs.

spots.name: Gallagher's Boxty House
spots.summary: Good traditional Irish fare and not expensive. A boxty is a traditional Irish potato pancake filled and rolled up. Also try the Irish stew and the chowder. Small, friendly, traditional Irish decor.

spots.name: Frank Ryans

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This pub and pizzeria has friendly bar staff and a mixed crowd of students, law types, trendies and locals. Expect weekly trad nights interspersed with Rockabilly, Country and Soul on the jukebox.

spots.name: Butlers Chocolate Café
spots.summary: Chain of chocolate-themed cafes, Wicklow Street is the original outlet. There are three others in city centre, plus airside in T1 and T2 at the airport. They also ship orders.

spots.name: Against the Grain

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Owned by a Galway brewery, this has a wide variety of Irish micro-brews and world beers. No generic commercial beers on tap. A vibrant pub with an eclectic clientele.

spots.name: The Oval

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: Good for drink and food, does an excellent Irish stew. Attracts a mixed age group. Lots of pictures of old Irish celebrities with a tribute to the Quiet Man.

spots.name: Bewley's Café
spots.summary: Grand stylish coffee shop, a Dublin institution. It's had some famous regular customers, from Joyce to Geldof, but they'll make you feel just as important.

spots.name: The Lotts

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Cafe bar, elegant interior with chandeliers, a marble bar and comfortable leather seating. Live music many nights. Small outside seating area.

spots.name: Grogan's

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: Wonderful trad pub, no music or TV. Great Guinness and a mixture of tourists and locals, with a hotchpotch of interesting art on the walls.

spots.name: Pablo Picante

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Small friendly Mexican eatery, eat in or take away to nearby St Stephen's Green. They also have outlets at Clarendon Market and Dawson St.

spots.name: Zaytoon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Casual Persian restaurant. They also have a fast-food cafe in Temple Bar (corner of Parliament St and Essex St).

spots.name: Caketopia

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Artisan home-made cakes for any occasion for collection or delivery all over Dublin and surrounding areas.

spots.name: Kites

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Chinese, predominantly Cantonese, also in Szechuan, Peking and Thai style, gets great reviews.

spots.name: Brasserie Sixty6

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Large, stylish modern European restaurant gets good reviews for food, service and atmosphere.

spots.name: Bad Ass Café

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri

spots.summary: Modern pub and entertainment venue for US-themed food, plus trad Irish beer and live music.

spots.name: Bang Restaurant

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A great cosmopolitan menu. Not cheap, but food and presentation is excellent.

spots.name: Fire Steakhouse

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Casual dining restaurant in the former Supper Room of the Lord Mayor.

spots.name: Cornucopia
spots.summary: Smart modern restaurant for vegan and other wholefood options.
